blocks.content: Every replica in a StatefulSet gets its own predictable, stable DNS name that persists across restarts and rescheduling, even though, exactly as covered in the Pod Replacement topic, its actual IP address still changes.
1. Each Replica Gets Its Own Stable Name
blocks.text: 1. Each Replica Gets Its Own Stable Name

blocks.content: Unlike a Deployment's Pods, which are reachable only anonymously through a Service, each StatefulSet replica gets its own individually addressable DNS name, app-0 is always reachable as app-0, distinct from app-1.

blocks.alt: Each replica individually addressable, not merged into one anonymous pool

blocks.content: This is exactly the payoff of the headless Service covered in the Services module, its DNS lookup behavior (returning individual Pod IPs rather than one virtual IP) combined with StatefulSet's ordinal naming is precisely what makes per-replica addressing possible.

blocks.alt: The headless Service mechanism from the Services module, doing the real work here

blocks.content:
# Full DNS form for one specific StatefulSet replica
app-0.app-headless.default.svc.cluster.local

blocks.content: 3. Identity Persists, Even Though the IP Still Changes
blocks.text: 3. Identity Persists, Even Though the IP Still Changes

blocks.content: This is the genuinely important distinction from ordinary Pods, exactly as covered in the Pod Replacement topic, a replaced Pod still gets a new IP address, but a StatefulSet replica's name, and therefore its DNS identity, stays exactly the same across that replacement.

blocks.alt: The IP still changes on replacement, but the name and DNS identity do not

blocks.content: Distributed, coordinated systems often need to reliably find the same specific peer again, "which node is currently the primary" is a question that needs a stable answer, ordinary Pod IPs cannot provide that, stable per-replica DNS names can.

blocks.alt: A stable answer to "which specific peer is this," something ordinary Pods cannot offer

blocks.content: The full DNS form, app-0.app-headless.namespace.svc.cluster.local, resolves to exactly one specific Pod, not a load-balanced group, this precision is exactly what distinguishes it from an ordinary Service's DNS entry.

blocks.alt: One name, resolving to one specific, individually identified Pod

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Each StatefulSet replica gets its own stable DNS name via a headless Service, individually addressable, not anonymously load-balanced like ordinary Pods.
This identity persists across a replica's IP changing on replacement, exactly what distributed, coordinated systems need to reliably find the same specific peer again.
